correctness.rationale: The eighteen-vertex cubic incidence graph has every paired-dominating set even. Degree lower bound and explicit six-vertex matched dominating cores establish \(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}=6\). Both the incidence-bitmask and coordinate-bijection verifiers enumerate exactly the nine six-vertex cores and exactly 216 feasible balanced eight-vertex sets. The 108-affine-map orbit certificate exhausts all 126 four-point choices, with line choice counts 12,0,0,0 on orbits of sizes 18,27,54,27. Equality with the explicit nine-core-by-24-extension template is asserted for the full candidate domain. The perfect-matching cases are direct or crossed through one matched core edge; the exclusion graph on six points and six lines is exactly a spanning 12-cycle, hence the allowed graph is \(K_{6,6}-C_{12}\). Single-vertex swaps become edge incidence in that allowed graph, so each component is its line graph, with 24 vertices, degree six, 72 edges and diameter three. Between-core swaps are impossible. The actual scripts and output files are bundled and replayed; the proof makes no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches of mathematical records, conventional literature, graph-specific aliases, and accessible earlier work produced no claim that entails the exact nine-component eight-vertex paired-domination jump graph. The closest universal 2017 gamma_pr construction uses minimum placements and slides and does not give the Pappus eight-vertex graph. A 2023 paired-domination dissertation covers explicitly listed families, not Pappus, and its full-text Pappus search returned no match; its actual relevant sections were inspected. A contemporary Franklin-graph scalar paired-domination calculation cannot entail this fixed graph line-graph isomorphism. Unindexed equivalent work remains possible; publisher access to the complete 1998 foundational article was unavailable, but that paper is used as origin of the definition, not declared non-covering based on its abstract. The finite result is judged new only to the extent of the specified bounded searches.
residual_risks: An equivalent jump graph classification might appear in unindexed or non-English published literature.
The full publisher text of the 1998 origin paper was not obtained; its abstract cannot establish any whole-document negative.
The inspected 2023 dissertation was searched digitally and selected relevant pages were read, not all 122 pages exhaustively read.

value.rationale: This is an exact connectivity classification for a canonical cubic bipartite incidence graph under a natural constrained replacement process. The jump from nine frozen minimum paired-dominating configurations to nine 24-vertex mobile sectors after exactly two extra placements is mathematically meaningful. Uniquely recoverable cores give a geometric obstruction, while the line-graph identification yields precise reachability and diameter. This is not a routine substitution in a known domination formula, a recomputation of the graph domination number, or an arbitrary unmotivated parameter slice. Generalization beyond order three is explicitly not asserted.
